title: SOFTWARE ENGINEER
tagline: Full-stack software engineering, end to end
summary: Full-stack software engineering — real products shipped the whole way through, from database schema and backend APIs to the interface someone actually uses.
description: I build products the whole way through — database schema, backend APIs, and the interface someone actually uses. My primary stack is React, Next.js, and Ruby on Rails, with PostgreSQL underneath.

This is the foundation everything else sits on. The ERP integration work, the systems architecture, the products I've shipped independently — all of it is built on the same core discipline: write backend logic that holds up under real use, and ship an interface that doesn't get in the way.

title: ERP INTEGRATION SPECIALIST
tagline: Connecting the enterprise systems that were never built to talk
summary: Connecting field-sales software to the ERPs that run the business — SAP Business One, Oracle, Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica, Sage, SYSPRO, Odoo, Tally, and Epicor iScala — so orders, invoices, prices, and stock move between them reliably.
description: For three years at Solutech I worked on the integrations between its Sales Automation Tool and clients' ERPs. Before the dedicated integrator existed, that meant SAP Business One and other ERPs wired directly into the platform: posting orders and sales invoices, pulling price lists, special prices, blanket agreements, and account status. I built the Acumatica connector from scratch.

Later I worked on the on-premise integrator that replaced those direct links — a configurable middleware layer that reads ERPs over ODBC or their own APIs and writes back through COM SDKs, REST, SOAP, or XML. There I built the Sage 200 Evolution API integration, order-status tracking through a database trigger and outbox, and a validator that checks every ERP query pack against a live schema. The hard part is never the API call; it's making two systems with different data models agree on what an order, a price, or a customer is.
